The Mongol conquests begin (ev.mongol-conquests); China's losses to them and to the Yuan collapse carry Asia's share down toward 1400.
China's own losses in the Yuan collapse bring Asia's share down after 1353.
Revised from 60.8 with the Americas' share, which no longer falls before smallpox reaches the mainland, so the five shares still sum to 100.
Rises only because the Americas' share falls, mid-epidemic in central Mexico.
Revised from 61.3 with the Americas' share, so the five shares still sum to 100. Rises only because the Americas' share falls.

Interpolated. Britain's first war in Burma and the Java War (some 200,000 Javanese dead) open the colonial century in South-east Asia. Asia's share eases because Europe's and the Americas' people grow faster, not because Asia's fall.

Interpolated. The El Niño famines of 1876 to 1879 kill perhaps 5 to 10 million in India and 9 to 13 million in north China on the usual estimates; Asia's share falls fastest in these decades, as Europe's and the Americas' people multiply while Asia's are cut back. The straight line spreads a loss that was concentrated in 1876 to 1879.
Asia's lowest share in two thousand years.

Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor and its conquest of South-east Asia (ev.sea.japanese-occupation, ev.oc.pacific-war): Asia's share holds near 55% through the war. China's war dead and the famines of Henan (1942 to 1943), Bengal (1943), Java and northern Vietnam (1944 to 1945) are set against Europe's heavier losses for its size and Southern and Western Asia's growth; the share moves by hundredths, not points.

The fall of Saigon and the Khmer Rouge's victory. Their killing and starving of perhaps a quarter of Cambodia's people, 1.5 to 2 million by 1979, takes about a twentieth of a point from Asia's share; Asia's births keep the share rising.
Vietnam takes Phnom Penh and ends the Khmer Rouge's rule, and China's war on Vietnam follows. Asia's share keeps rising: its deaths have fallen faster than its births.
The Indian Ocean tsunami kills about 230,000, a few thousandths of a point of humanity; Asia's share stands near its peak as births fall across East and South-east Asia.
India overtakes China as the most populous country (ev.as.india-most-populous); Asia's share keeps easing as Africa's grows.
Grotte Mandrin in the Rhône valley may hold a brief Homo sapiens presence about 54,000 years ago, among Neanderthals; debated, and with no lasting population.
The Aurignacians of the Danube and the Swabian Jura, with the first figurines and flutes, and Chauvet's paintings about 36,000 years ago.
South-west France, the Franco-Cantabrian refuge, holds Western Europe's people at the glacial maximum; the north and the Alps are empty.
The Linear Pottery farmers spread from the Danube across the loess of Germany and northern France, about 5500 to 5000 BCE.
Celtic Gaul before Caesar's conquest, perhaps six to eight million.
Late Roman Gaul and the Rhineland, after the third-century crisis and before the Rhine frontier breaks at the end of 406.
The high-medieval clearing of forests in France and Germany: Western Europe becomes Europe's largest part.
France perhaps 17 to 20 million, the most populous kingdom in Christendom, before the great famine of 1315 and the plague.
The Black Death (ev.black-death).
Interpolated: France's wars of religion (from 1562) and the Dutch revolt (from 1568) kill hundreds of thousands, yet Western Europe's numbers keep pace with the world's.

Interpolated: the Thirty Years' War begins (1618). Most of Germany's losses to war, plague and hunger, perhaps a third of its people, fall in the 1630s; the value is kept on the line between its neighbours so Europe's parts still sum to Europe, and the band holds a later fall.
The Thirty Years War (1618 to 1648) costs Germany perhaps a third of its people, in some regions more than half, to war, plague and hunger.
The French Revolution begins. France's births have begun to fall, and its wars from 1792 to 1815 kill about a million and a half French soldiers on most estimates, so Western Europe's share eases.
France's births begin to fall a century before the rest of Europe's, and Western Europe's share eases from here.

Interpolated: industry spreads from Britain to Belgium, northern France and the Rhineland, and the first factory laws pass; Western Europe's share holds while France's births stay low and Germany's rise.
The Western Front: France and Germany each lose more than a million and a half soldiers.
Some twelve million Germans expelled from the east arrive in the occupied zones, 1945 to 1950.
Immigration, the refugees of 2015 and of Ukraine since 2022 among them, keeps Germany's and France's numbers rising while their births stay low.

Sahul before people on the later arrival, about 50,000 years ago; luminescence dates at Madjedebe of about 65,000 years would put people here already. The two accounts are debated (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b).
Zero here takes the later arrival in Sahul (about 50,000 years); Madjedebe's 65,000 would make it positive.

Interpolated: Sahul's first people reach New Guinea's highlands (the Ivane valley) and Arnhem Land's ground-edge axes by about 49,000 years ago. When they first arrived is debated, about 65,000 years ago on Madjedebe's dates or about 50,000 on others; this series takes the later date, and the band carries both.
Sahul's first people spread across the continent and New Guinea (ev.oc.sahul-arrival, ev.oc.lake-mungo).
Interpolated: people reach Tasmania across the Bass Strait land bridge and the Bismarcks and Solomons by sea, and bury their dead at Lake Mungo; Sahul's share rises as its people fill the continent.
Sahul's people keep growing as they settle its margins and highlands after the megafauna are gone (ev.oc.megafauna-extinction).

Interpolated: Australia's mid-Holocene changes (new tools, Pama-Nyungan's spread, eel traps at Budj Bim) and New Guinea's gardens add people, but farmers elsewhere multiply faster, so Oceania's share keeps falling.

Interpolated: Lapita voyagers reach the Bismarcks and then Remote Oceania, and voyagers from Island South-east Asia settle Palau and the Marianas; new islands add people, but too few to turn the share.

The value stands but is debated: the usual pre-contact estimates (Aboriginal Australians from about 300,000 to over a million, Maori about 100,000, Melanesia one to two million, Polynesia and Micronesia some hundreds of thousands) sum to about 2 to 3.5 million, 0.4 to 0.7% of the world's people in 1500 and 0.25 to 0.35% in 1788, against this series' 0.2%, about 0.9 to 2 million (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b). The band now carries both; moving the value needs Asia's and Europe's shares rebalanced with it.

The First Fleet lands at Sydney (ev.oc.first-fleet); smallpox and the frontier wars begin to cut Aboriginal numbers while settlers are still few. The usual pre-contact estimates would put Oceania at 0.25 to 0.35% here; the band carries them.
Before gold is found: about 2.5 million people in Oceania, some 0.47 million of them settlers in Australia and New Zealand and about 2 million islanders and first peoples.
The gold rushes (ev.oc.gold-rushes) nearly double Australia's settlers in four years.
Corrected from 0.2, which left the gold rushes out: settlers reach about 1.1 million against roughly 2 million first peoples and islanders.
Corrected from 0.2: Otago's rush (1861) adds New Zealand's settlers to Australia's.
Corrected from 0.2: about 1.6 million settlers.
Corrected from 0.22: about 1.9 million settlers, while the first peoples keep falling (ev.oc.depopulation).

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"observation","text":"Between -151000 and -127000 sea level rises 110 m, temperature 6 °C, CO2 from 190 to 275 ppm and forest from 36 to 47% of land. This is Termination II, into the Last Interglacial, warmer than pre-industrial and with seas several metres higher. Humanity's numbers are guessed to rise with it (0.35 to 0.5 million), because a green Sahara and Arabia opened ranges that the glacial had closed. The early sapiens fossils outside Africa, such as Misliya and Skhul, fall in or near such windows; the model has no regional processes yet to show it."}
upsertNodes.title: The sharpest change at the finest level: the end of the penultimate glacial
Second pass of history as numbers: levels 3 and 4 of the time schedule

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"The first pass gave the eight religion shares as anchors at -300000 and -1000 and interpolated them linearly onto its dates. Between those anchors that put 1.3% of people in the Hindu tradition and 0.9% in Chinese traditions 100,000 years ago, and 3% Hindu in 5000 BCE: no one claimed this, the arithmetic did. Every share before 1000 BCE is now local and folk traditions at 100%, at the old dates and the new. The jump to the anchor at -1000 (95, 3, 0, 2) now stands for the Vedic and Zhou traditions forming, which is a claim. The general lesson for whoever fills next: interpolating between anchors far apart makes claims about the dates between, so guess those dates instead."}
upsertNodes.title: Religion shares before 1000 BCE were an interpolation artefact

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"Time -10000 is about 12,000 years before present, inside the Younger Dryas. Global reconstructions of the deglaciation, Shakun and colleagues' as recalled, reach Holocene levels only about 10,000 years ago. The first pass's -1.5 °C put the world most of the way there two thousand years early. The new -12000 value (-3.5 °C, the Bølling–Allerød) and -7900 (-0.8 °C) are guessed around the revised one."}

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"observation","text":"Filling 54 blocks, rather than interpolating, put shapes into the curves that the coarser dates had smoothed over.

- Population is not monotone: it falls at 1400 after the Black Death and is nearly flat from 1 CE to 770 through the Antonine, Cyprianic and Justinianic plagues and the fall of the Han. MalthusianTrap#0f6b predicts output per person should rise after each loss; the values do it after 1348 (850 to 900) but barely after 200 CE, which is a question rather than a confirmation: either the late-antique losses fell on output too (trade and cities shrank, habitat 5 to 4.5) or the provisioning values there are too flat.
- War, being averaged to the next date, changes meaning when a date is inserted. The Mongol conquests now sit in a 1140–1300 average of 50 per 100,000, the end of the Taiping war and the Dungan revolt in 1859–1890 at 40. The 1850 value (50) now covers only 1850–1859, when Taiping deaths were heaviest, and is probably too low.
- Heights fall to a trough near 3900–2200 BCE and recover over three millennia: DensityRatchet#2ace's longer hours and poorer health, held in place by the numbers farming fed.
- Energy per person barely moves between 1 CE (15 GJ) and 1820 (21 GJ), then doubles by 1900: Sunbound#c94c, as expected.
- The largest polity peaks as a share of humanity under the Qing around 1820 (35%), higher than any empire before.

No contradiction was reported between any parent declaring an aggregate and its children (safety is the sum of homicide and war at every date)."}
upsertNodes.title: What the finest level shows

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"This pass is done by the coverage report: four levels, 3,650 values, no empty, flat or contradictory process. Left for another pass:

1. Events. The account has none below History. The shocks it already shows (the deglaciation, the spread of farming, the plagues of 165, 541 and 1347, the Mongol conquests, 1492, the world wars, Concorde) should become Events naming the processes they move. It can wait because the series already carry their effects; Events add the why.
2. Divide the processes never divided, highest first: carbon dioxide, forest, sea level, continuation, exchange. The structure construction (structure/history-tree.mjs) already has carves for most of them; this construction's 50 processes predate that alignment.
3. Check the root's rival accounts. claude.hypothesis.ever-born names what would decide between 64 and 117 billion ever born: palaeodemographic life expectancy. Until then the band holds both.
4. Revisit war in 1850–1859, and provisioning in late antiquity (see claude.observation.level4).
5. Check the inferred values after 1500 against their sources (UN WPP, Maddison, Our World in Data, the Law Dome core): every one is recalled, so EvidenceDependence#23ca applies, and none is tagged source.
6. Places. Every process is world-level; the M49 regions are the next resolution."}
upsertNodes.title: Left for another pass, and why each can wait

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"h.connection asks for the fastest regular passenger speed. The first pass held it at 900 km/h from 1960 to 2025, the subsonic jet. Concorde flew scheduled services at about Mach 2 from January 1976 to October 2003, so the values at 1980, 1985, 1990, 1996 and 2000 are now 2,150. The series then falls back to 900 at 2006: the fastest regular speed went down, one of the few reversals in the account. A reading must answer the question as it is worded (MetricReading#56a9, failure mode 'definition mismatch'): the first pass read 'regular' as 'mass'. If the intended question is the speed most travellers could reach, that is a different series with its own question, not a reinterpretation of this one.","data":{"sema":["sema:MetricReading#mh:SHA-256:56a9f18faad70147312f12c1cdb1bcea9cb5d1d61042831d1fe6bfa11414ab26"]}}

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"analysis","text":"Regularity, from MalthusianTrap#0f6b: a pandemic that removes a large share of a population raises output per person in that population until numbers recover.

Test against the model's three pre-modern pandemics. World output per person (h.provisioning) is 800 in 1 CE and 790 in 200 around the Antonine plague, 750 in 500 and 760 in 770 around the Justinianic plague, and 830 in 1346, 880 in 1353 and 900 in 1400 around the Black Death. Only the Black Death shows the rise.

The flat cases are not evidence against the trap. The prediction is about the stricken population, and the series is a world aggregate. The Antonine plague struck the Roman empire, about a quarter of humanity, while Han China's collapse (184–280), a separate loss of output, fell in the same years: the two cancel in the world total. As recalled, Egyptian real wages rose after both the Antonine and the Justinianic plagues (Scheidel's wage series), which is the trap's prediction at the right scale. The Black Death shows at world level because it struck the Mediterranean, Europe and the Middle East together, a larger share of humanity.

DistinguishingTest#0439: a regional series of output per person for the Roman and Byzantine Mediterranean, held beside China's. The trap predicts a rise after 165 and 541 in the first and none in the second. Until regions exist in the model the regularity is held as exploring, supported only by the Black Death, and this is the strongest argument yet for opening the M49 regions."}
upsertNodes.title: Do pandemics raise output per person? The world series cannot tell

1. Regions. The plague test (claude.analysis.plague-trap-test) and the dispersal both need them; world aggregates hide what regional shocks do. Start with population and output per person for the M49 regions, from 1 CE.
2. War as deaths per date block rather than a rate averaged to the next date, so refinement conserves it by construction (claude.decision.events).
3. Events for the other turns the curves show: the Axial-age religions (-490 to -90), the demographic transition after 1950, the green revolution, the end of serfdom and slavery (1861–1888), the democratic waves.
4. Still open from claude.plan.next-pass: divide CO2, forest and sea level; check the inferred post-1500 values against sources; decide the ever-born rival accounts."}

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"assessment","text":"The number test asked whether 64 billion people ever born by 2025 is right against the usual estimate of about 117 billion (Population Reference Bureau). The check, by period, using the model's own population and life expectancy:
- 1650 to 2025: the model adds about 22 billion, the Bureau about 23. They agree. Prediction (b) of claude.hypothesis.ever-born holds: 1950 to 2025 adds 9.4 billion here, about what UN birth counts give.
- 1 to 1650: the model adds about 20 billion, the Bureau about 39. The Bureau's 60 births per 1,000 for 1 to 1200 means a life expectancy near 17 years; the model's is 24 to 28.
- Before 1 CE: the model has about 22 billion, the Bureau about 55. The Bureau's 80 per 1,000 from 8000 BCE means a life expectancy near 12.5 years; the model's 25 to 30 gives 35 to 40 births per 1,000.
Prediction (c) holds: the accounts differ almost wholly before 1650. The difference is one assumption, the life expectancy of ancient and prehistoric people. Forager life tables (Gurven and Kaplan) give 21 to 37 years; Roman Egypt's census about 22 to 25; neither supports 12.5. Adopting 117 billion would make this model contradict its own life expectancy for ten thousand years, so the value stands at 63.8 billion. Its band is widened to 48 to 120 billion so both published accounts fall inside it. It stays exploring: the figures here are recalled from one corpus (EvidenceDependence#23ca), and what would decide it is a direct check of prehistoric life expectancy, not of births since 1650. If the Bureau's account were preferred, the place to change is h.alive before 1650, not this series.","data":{"sema":["sema:EvidenceDependence#23ca"],"byPeriod":{"model":{"before1CE":22.2,"1to1650":19.7,"1650to2025":22},"prbAsRecalled":{"before1CE":55,"1to1650":39,"1650to2025":23}}}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"The number test found two labels that claim more than they measure. Simply renaming them would have broken the tree, because the process labelled 'What matters to people' (h.ends) headed nine dimensions: staying alive, sustenance, belonging, understanding, play, standing, freedom, meaning, continuation. Renamed 'Development index', it would have put freedom and worship under an index of life, literacy and income. So:
- h.ends keeps its values and is relabelled 'Development index', a child of a new process.
- h.wants, 'What matters to people', heads the nine dimensions and the index, with a measure of its own: the share of people whose first want for their lives is survival. That is one answer of the number test's question of what people most want (survival / security / family and faith / freedom and self-expression). It is sketched before 1980 from how many lived near subsistence and read from values surveys after (exploring). It falls from about 65% before industry to 20% in 2025.
- h.belonging, people per household, is relabelled 'Household size'. Belonging is a person's reading of a group, not a world count, so the node now says what it holds; marriage age stays beneath it as how households form.
- h.meaning, the share in regular worship, is relabelled 'Regular worship'. The number test flags it the same way, though the request named only the first two.
Values are unchanged; only labels, meanings and ten decomposition edges changed. Readers of older views should know that 'What matters to people' meant the index before revision 13."}

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"criticism","text":"Three findings for the tools.
- Passing over Events. Adding cause Events made every process 'pass over' them wherever three or more Event boundaries fell between two of a process's dates. The report names only the most crowded stretch each time, so finding them all took enumeration by hand, and filling them took values at 16 new dates for all 56 processes. A full list of crowded stretches, or the threshold stated, would make it one step.
- One decomposition as a series. life_series_record with refersTo, which the guide names for a change that adds up, makes the Cut a series held to the whole time schedule (300,000 years), asking for 55 readings of a question about one change. Recording the Cut directly on the outcome Event with life_model_revise is the grammar's native form, and the coverage report accepts it.
- Answer keys. A key with a hyphen, or one named 'other', is refused with a message about remainders; underscores are required."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"question","text":"1. The dispersal's trigger. Why about 60,000 years ago, rather than with the earlier humid windows? A wetter window about 60,000 years ago was added as an Event and withdrawn the same day: late humid phases in Arabia rest on too few records. The dispersal question has two causes, and the condition that made this venture succeed is weakly evidenced (exploring).
2. Single causes. The Great Chinese Famine is read with policy alone, because weather's difference is small and a weather Event would crowd the schedule's 1950s stretch. COVID-19's toll is read with vaccines alone; distancing and treatment have no Events yet.
3. Additive divisions not yet made:
   - Poverty: the fall in people in extreme poverty by country, which fails because the number rose in sub-Saharan Africa while it fell in Asia, so the parts are not all of one sign.
   - Bondage: the fall in bondage by emancipation, which needs counts of the freed that the model lacks (India 1843 and the Habsburg and Prussian emancipations of 1848 are uncertain by factors of two).
   - Population: the people added since 1900 divided by cause rather than by region. A Bongaarts-type decomposition into momentum, high fertility and falling mortality would do it, but has not been worked out for the past.
4. Laws. The recurring causes (mass schooling, the second world war, the Little Ice Age) could become abstract relations between the mechanism concepts and the dimensions they couple; the model's own question about laws is still open."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"analysis","text":"Each new instance claim was made only after reading the card's invariants against the model's own values.
- DemographicTransition#6e31 holds at world scale.
  - Deaths fall first: child mortality 38% to 23% and life expectancy 32 to 46 between 1900 and 1950, while fertility moves only from 5.5 to 4.9.
  - Births follow after a lag: fertility stays near 5 until 1965, then falls to 2.2.
  - Growth peaks in the lag: 0.6% a year in 1900–1910, 1.9% in the 1950s, 2.05% in 1965–1970, then 1.45% in the 1990s and 0.9% in 2020–2025.
  - Its failure mode 'end assumed' applies: the world sits near replacement only as an average of Africa above 4 and East Asia below 1.2.
- MalthusianTrap#0f6b names its own end. From 1780 to 1910 the population doubles (0.91 to 1.75 billion) while output per person rises 2.2 times (1,120 to 2,500 dollars), which the card excludes. So the trap is broken in the model in the nineteenth century, not before. The relation 'the demographic transition ends the trap' records this, and Sunbound#c94c is related as what must be lifted first.
- DensityRatchet#2ace fits Haber–Bosch. Twinflow#9474 fits COVID-19's spread by air. Sunbound#c94c's lifting fits the escape from poverty, with warming as the card's 'new bounds ignored'.
- ExitCage#eef7 for the first states and CumulativeCulture#4f93 for the southern African toolkits stay exploring. Their key invariants (exit costs; dependence on population size and connection) are argued from the regional pattern, not measured in the model.
These answer the model's question about laws in part: the regularities are stated as concepts, their relations and claimed instances, and tested where the model has the numbers.","data":{"sema":["sema:DemographicTransition#mh:SHA-256:6e31f50b19556b5b9d064d144b5d38ad11b5035daefc2c7d335a798f6f5e7023","sema:MalthusianTrap#0f6b","sema:DensityRatchet#2ace","sema:Twinflow#mh:SHA-256:947477acf8435fa11be8a39a4d344d688445401036944becd6af0636d8f705f0","sema:Sunbound#mh:SHA-256:c94c74970e9c2f8954dfd44e3844fc69bcda69ee43b8adda10c645c7e8e99764","sema:ExitCage#mh:SHA-256:eef79b28d91f7a5904c5526d70d0a0b3aa60e68b5fd2641420e425c848bd676b","sema:CumulativeCulture#mh:SHA-256:4f938b644cc8fd33afd520ea0e9c04e43b8156908b2db513a638e053f7e86dbe"]}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"The first round found that conditions usually outweigh the triggers that set outcomes off. Two readings added in this round refine that.
- For the Holocene the trigger is largest. The orbital rise in northern summer sunlight makes a difference of 0.92; the deglaciation's feedbacks, which made it work, 0.75.
- For the Second World War, condition and trigger are close. The First World War's unsettled peace makes 0.55 and the Depression and the regimes it brought to power 0.5.
The pattern: a trigger dominates when it is an outside forcing that recurs on its own schedule, like the orbit, and the condition (ice sheets large enough to collapse) is common in the contrast period. A condition dominates when it is rare in the contrast and triggers are common, as for the Holocene before farming, coal before industry, or isolation before the Columbian collapse. This is ContrastClass#7398 again: what is rare in the foil does the explaining.","data":{"sema":["sema:ContrastClass#mh:SHA-256:7398dcd341662f9a871586de9037c08c6a825113c47694f18d764e353ba55a77"]}}

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Continuing construction/after-causes.construction.json (head graph 00b63098, model r34 07d31b6d) on 2026-10-12, with the live viewer open and Sema in use. The import was verified (18 graph revisions, 35 models). The tools served here are the Meaning Model 0.11.0 engine and a Sema 0.10.0 vocabulary of 617 patterns (store/sema/world-history-0.10.0.db), not the 0.9.0 and 0.8.0 that tool.json pins; the hashes in this pass are those of 0.11.0.

The account had the structure, the numbers and the causes of the turning points, but 91 Events, almost all world-scale. This pass fills in the Events of each era, each region and each dimension, from the long run to the short:
1. Places and categories (r35, r36). Humanity and the Earth become Things with lifecycles inside History. The Earth's land opens by UN M49 into six regions, seventeen subregions and seven intermediate regions, each a Thing whose lifecycle is its history. The twelve dimensions of structure/history-tree.mjs, with the Earth as setting, become concepts.
2. Humanity's ages and eras (r37): four ages, twelve eras partitioning them, and the existing Events re-filed in the innermost one whose interval holds theirs (Nestmap#8b8f: each Event names the larger situations it sits inside).
3. Each region's own eras, its own periodization rather than the world's, then the regional Events inside them, longest first.
4. Finer world Events inside humanity's eras.
5. For every Event: where, what, how important, part of what, what it led to, and its sources.
6. Causes for the Events that turn a measure, read as the causes pass did, against a stated contrast (ContrastClass#7398).
7. Values at the new Events' dates where they move a process, until the coverage report is done again.

The shape of an Event's record, so a website can draw timelines by region and by dimension at each level of detail:
- When: its interval; an Event dated only to a year or a decade keeps that span, and its description says so.
- Where: a located_in binding to each M49 region it happened in, and to the subregion or intermediate region where that is known. An Event in several regions has several. The free-text region field repeats it in words.
- What it belongs to: a describe Realization of its dimension's concept, with parameters.principal true for the dimension it belongs to first. Where an Event's properties point to more than one dimension it gets a Realization for each, principal false for the others (Labelsqueeze#5363: each candidate category is listed with what points to it, rather than forcing one label silently). At most three, so the classification still discriminates.
- How important: a level on the scale for everyone (importance.everyone), on the scale of each region it happened in (importance.region.*), and on the scale of each dimension it belongs to (importance.dim.*). The rarity levels top_10, top_100, top_1000 and noted are the levels of detail.
- Part of: a contains relation from the innermost Event it lies within: an era of humanity's history for an Event that changed humanity as a whole or several regions; an era of a region's history for one that belongs to that region; a longer Event where it is a part of one (smallpox in the Americas inside the Columbian exchange).
- Led to: causes, enables, prevents or constrains relations to later Events, each with a description.
- What it changed: process_ids names the processes it moves, as before, each with a value at its date.
- Sources: provenance begins with its tag and reason; a second entry names sources to check. Following README.md, a named source is where a recalled claim is to be checked, not a document that was read, and nothing is tagged source until one has been.

Why each process now names its Thing: the coverage report holds a process about the world in general to every Event, so hundreds of regional Events would have asked world carbon dioxide or world population for a value between every three of them. A process about one Thing is held to that Thing's Events and to the Events that name it. The world measures are about humanity, the Earth's about the Earth, and each regional share about its region, so a regional Event that does change a world measure names it and is held to it, while the founding of Mali does not ask the world's carbon dioxide for a value.

Guarding against what survives (SurvivorCorrect#3780): written records over-represent literate states, so each region's Events include foragers, herders and peoples known from archaeology, genetics or oral history, with that evidence named. {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"125 of the 676 Events had no located_in binding (the count of README.md, which treats the 30 place lifecycles as placed by their lifecycle binding): History, the lifecycles of the Earth and of humanity, humanity's four ages and fourteen eras, the 48 eras of the regions' own histories, and 56 world Events from the first passes. - What happened everywhere people lived is placed in the Earth as a whole (referent.earth): the ages and world eras after the dispersal, the mortality, fertility, schooling and literacy transitions, the climate's own changes, the fossil-fuel age, nuclear weapons, the postwar order. 55 Events.
- What happened in some regions is placed in each of them rather than forced into one or lifted to the Earth (Labelsqueeze#5363: each candidate region is listed with what in the description points to it). The Natufian, wild cereals and Mesopotamian irrigation in Western Asia; Still Bay and Howiesons Poort in Southern Africa; the first states in Western and Southern Asia and Northern Africa; the slave trade in western and west-central Africa, the Caribbean, Latin and Northern America and Europe; decolonization in Asia, Africa, the Caribbean and Oceania; temperate clearing across Northern and South America, Eastern Europe (all of Russia counts in Europe by M49), Southern and Eastern Asia and Australia; foragers in Africa, with their brief ventures, in Africa and Western Asia; the dispersal era in Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania, before the Americas were reached.

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"1. The Second World War is now a shape, not a step. War deaths run at about 150 per 100,000 a year in 1940 and the first half of 1941, then about 650 from the invasion of the Soviet Union through 1944, and 500 in 1945's last months of war. Life expectancy dips from 40 (1940) to about 36.5 (1944) before the war's end lifts it to 41 within months and 46 by 1950; the development index dips with it. That dip is the famines of Bengal, Henan and Vietnam as much as the fighting.
2. The first globalization peaks on the eve of the First World War: trade at about 11.5% of output and coal-age energy at 34 GJ a person in 1913-14, neither regained until the 1950s.
3. Debates now stated beside their values rather than decided: whether Toba's eruption cooled the climate or thinned Asia's early sapiens for more than a few years; whether people reached Sahul by 65,000 years ago (Madjedebe) or about 50,000 (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b); and the conquest of the Americas told as smallpox together with war and forced labour, not disease alone (VirginSoilEpidemic#d1fd, its failure mode 'germs absolve').
4. Several regional catastrophes are still on the line in the regional shares, because the shares were filled coarse and the Events came later: the Ming-Qing transition (1618-1683) leaves Asia's share rising, the Great Leap famine (1959-61) is not visible in it, and the Thirty Years War not in Europe's. Each is a place where a finer reading would turn the curve.","data":{"semaRefs":["sema:EvidenceUnderdetermination#mh:SHA-256:999b3244c9eb73cf0968148e4ff5dd11e3abc42330ed5faafe618af972079e28","sema:VirginSoilEpidemic#mh:SHA-256:d1fd811afceaea483fe483c103b1c668e86d518625f8735bfa6328923597e878"]}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"model","text":"The coverage report holds a process about humanity to every Event in humanity's lifecycle and every Event that names it, a process about the Earth to the Earth's, and each regional share to its region's; it says a process passes over its Events when three or more of them begin strictly between two of its values. With engine 0.12.0 the finest level of the time schedule also asks for a value near each Thing's own Events, thinned to one per fifty-fourth of the span: the Last Interglacial's opening (-130000) for humanity, Toba (-72100) for the Earth, the Denisovans, Neanderthal minds and Pinnacle Point for Asia, Europe and Africa. That is where the 57 missing values came from, after the previous pass had been done by the older engine.
- Humanity's measures share one date grid, so one set of dates broke every crowded stretch: -130000, -9500, -3500, -1200, -800, -500, 610, 1206, 1450, 1789, 1914.6, 1941.5, 1944, 1945.7, 1946.5 and 2002, skipped where a process already had a value close enough, with process-specific dates where an Event names the process: -550 and -221 for the largest polity (the Achaemenids, Qin), -268 and 65 for Buddhism (Ashoka, the arrival in China), 960 for Christianity and local traditions (the north's conversion), 618 and 960 for the largest city (the Tang, the Song), 1917.15 and 1949.75 for no religion (the Russian revolution, the People's Republic), 1948.3 for wants (Europe's postwar boom), 2001.95 for trade (China joins the WTO).
- Each region was worked through against its own set. A region's lifecycle contains Events filed under other regions: Asia's holds the Austronesian expansion with Lapita and the Polynesian settlements, the Crusades and gunpowder; Europe's holds the Second World War with its theatres, the industrial revolution and Columbus; so their shares needed values at those too (Asia 43, Europe 30, Africa 24, the Americas 12, Oceania 4).
- A value at a date where nothing moves the process is interpolated on the line between its recorded neighbours, so the curve says the Event did not change it; that needs no note. Where an Event does move it, the value departs from the line and its note names the Event: the war years' dip in life expectancy, food and the development index, the 1913 peak of trade and output, Japan's and Italy's 1946 elections in democracy, forced labour's 1944 peak.
- War is a rate averaged to the next date, so a new date inside a block re-splits that block's average and the earlier value is revised to keep the total: 1940's 500 (to 1945.7) becomes 150 to mid-1941, 650 to 1944, 650 to 1945 and 500 to 1945.7, the same 2,850 per 100,000 over the stretch; 1780's 12 becomes 7 to 1789 and 16 to 1800. Violent deaths follow as homicide plus war.
- Bands accompany every new value, the neighbours' relative width where nothing new is known, and every value carries its tag: sketch before 1500 as its neighbours, inferred after, exploring for people ever born and for wants from 1985.","data":{"models":["r59 e2323a39acb1","r60 c0eb14dfe07a","r61 fb69d35fcbb0","r62 cb5538d3cd0c","r63 7b253b559a26"],"newDatesForHumanity":[-130000,-9500,-3500,-1200,-800,-500,610,1206,1450,1789,1914.6,1941.5,1944,1945.7,1946.5,2002]}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Continuing at graph r28 (788173e0), model r63 (7b253b55), on 2026-10-14, with the Meaning Model 0.12.0 engine and the project's Sema 0.10.0 vocabulary (store/sema/world-history.db, 617 patterns), read back first through life_construction_replay and life_model_outline. This pass fills out the history of the Americas; the tree of processes stays as it is (no process opened, none filed under another).

What the reading showed:
- The Americas' lifecycle holds 86 Events, against Africa's 143, Asia's 178 and Europe's 153 (Oceania, with a fiftieth of the people, has 48). Only one Americas outcome, the domestication of squash and maize, has weighed causes; the Americas' rise from 2.6% to 13.9% of humanity has none, though Asia's, Africa's and Europe's turns were weighed.
- The lifecycles of Northern America, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Caribbean, Central America and South America are empty: every Event sits in one of nine hemisphere-wide eras.
- Those eras use Mesoamerica's periodization (Archaic, Formative, Classic, Postclassic) for the whole hemisphere. Checked against what filing in an era asserts (Situfit#74e5), Cahokia in 'the Postclassic' shares the date, not the features: Northern America's own sequence is Archaic, Woodland and Mississippian; the Andes' is the Initial Period, the horizons and the intermediate periods; the Caribbean's is Archaic, Saladoid, Ostionoid and Taíno. That is why 21 Events (the Aztec, Caral, Chaco, the Inca and others) sat directly in the Americas' lifecycle: they straddle boundaries drawn for another region.

The plan, from the long run to the short:
1. Each subregion its own eras, in the periodization its own historians use, from the first arrivals to 2025: Northern America; the Caribbean, Central America and South America (M49's intermediate regions of Latin America); and Latin America and the Caribbean from 1492, when its parts begin a shared colonial and national history. Before 1492 it is not one history, so its eras start there.
2. Re-file every Americas Event in the innermost frame whose place and time hold it (Nestmap#8b8f, nearest situation first): an Event of one intermediate region or subregion in that region's era; one across Latin America in Latin America's era; one across the hemisphere in the Americas' era, which stays as the hemisphere's frame. The old contains relation is replaced, not doubled; an Event that is also part of a longer Event keeps that link. An Event that crosses its region's era boundary is contained by the region's lifecycle, as the events pass did.
3. Then the Events inside each era, longest first, with foragers, Arctic, Amazonian and Caribbean peoples known from archaeology, genetics and oral history, and Indigenous history after 1492 as well as colonial history (SurvivorCorrect#3780).
4. For every Event, the events pass's record shape: located_in to the Americas and to its subregion or intermediate region; Realizations of one to three dimensions, principal first (Labelsqueeze#5363); a level on everyone's scale, the Americas' scale, each dimension's scale and any other region it touched; contains from what it is part of; causes, enables, prevents or constrains to what it led to; sources to check in the provenance, which names where a recalled claim is to be checked, not a document that was read.
5. The causes of the turning points, weighed against stated contrasts (ContrastClass#7398), with the share questions set against growth at the world's rate (BaseRateInclude#1e63) as for the other regions, and debates stated with their alternatives (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b).
6. Values only where an Event moves a measure: the cocoliztli epidemics of 1545 and 1576 in the Americas' share of humanity, the jet airliner in the fastest regular passenger speed; existing turns that a new Event explains get a note naming it. Stretches that new Events pass over are left for the last pass of the night, which brings the coverage report back to done.
7. The graph is rebound after every model revision.

Recalled figures here share one foundation (EvidenceDependence#23ca); dates and tolls are given as usually stated, with contested ones marked, and judged by consequence for later lives rather than fame (HindsightBlock#5d8d).","data":{"schema":"world-history-pass-plan/v1","semaPatterns":["sema:Situfit#mh:SHA-256:74e56492432fc6fc7dafcdd9304e0654998b47f336371c5e665a49e35f605369","sema:Nestmap#mh:SHA-256:8b8f409b40e98c43817e4ee50d81d4c93ac62a614cb89ddb34087ddb0aef6437","sema:SurvivorCorrect#mh:SHA-256:37802a37d7e4bc9080836e17c5fbf7c170bce0942ed40d8a4960c46f6ca2407c","sema:Labelsqueeze#mh:SHA-256:5363fd96234c9745a73f11e01c75c07f119428b593daffaf617233a817607ac0","sema:ContrastClass#mh:SHA-256:7398dcd341662f9a871586de9037c08c6a825113c47694f18d764e353ba55a77","sema:BaseRateInclude#mh:SHA-256:1e637d4655d2b503d5cc333935aa74aabb13d09f174577f4d6cdf0de77688569","sema:EvidenceUnderdetermination#mh:SHA-256:999b3244c9eb73cf0968148e4ff5dd11e3abc42330ed5faafe618af972079e28","sema:EvidenceDependence#mh:SHA-256:23ca19433d2e0bf6109a8334ef2a6d8a42124a01a802d5a8fe0c9a049a7b5582","sema:HindsightBlock#mh:SHA-256:5d8d82eb55fe76c2657aa1f5ac21d4bc38edb2a3835c4e1ca1a071bad5f2a8fd"],"startGraph":"788173e0465031003a356d928a0500d62baebd7ab228adfc63c6713c91ba258f","startModel":"7b253b559a26236560c79107a4b862932f703020f81b5fac04563d4f36c9988a"}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"analysis","text":"Findings of the Americas pass, at model r77 (3d06e9a03635). Every reading below is tagged sketch, with sources to check in its provenance.

1. The frame. The hemisphere-wide eras used Mesoamerica's periodization for every subregion. Tested against what filing in an era asserts (Situfit#74e5), they shared dates but not features. The subregions now have their own eras, and each Event sits in the innermost frame whose place and time hold it (Nestmap#8b8f):
- Northern America, 8 eras: Paleo-Indian, Archaic, Woodland, Mississippian, colonies and Native nations, republic, industry, world power.
- The Caribbean, 8 eras: first islanders, Saladoid, Ostionoid and Taíno, the Spanish Caribbean, the sugar islands, emancipation, the American century, independent and dependent islands.
- Central America, 9 eras: Mesoamerica's own sequence to 1521, then New Spain, the republics, revolution, and the crisis since 1979.
- South America, 12 eras: the Andean Preceramic, the Initial Period, the horizons and the intermediate periods, then colonial, the republics, state-led development, and democracy.
- Latin America and the Caribbean, 5 eras from 1492, when its parts begin a shared history.
With these frames, what remains directly in a lifecycle crosses its own region's boundaries: for example the north-west coast's ranked societies, the Hohokam, the Mapuche, the Kalinago, Haiti's independence debt, the Great Migration and the residential schools. The hemisphere's nine eras keep what crossed the hemisphere: the Monroe Doctrine, the drug trade, migration north and NAFTA.
The new Events add the peoples a conquest-centred list leaves out (SurvivorCorrect#3780): Arctic, Amazonian, Caribbean and Plains peoples, and Indigenous history after 1492 alongside colonial and national history. Amazonia's towns and earthworks and Brazil's shell mounds are among them. The forest's poor preservation is not evidence of few people (AbsenceEvidence#10a3).

2. The causes. There are ten questions, each against a stated contrast (ContrastClass#7398), with 32 readings. Where a point is debated, the question's provenance states the debate (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b).
- The peopling (why.612f98622b725b75c7261e47). The retreat of the ice that opened a way south ranks first (0.75). The glacial maximum's ice, which held people in Beringia through the long pause the genomes show, is the other face of the same contrast. Whether people were south of the ice before it, as the White Sands footprints suggest, stays a stated debate.
- The Classic Maya collapse (why.e526f1e44b8a7828185aa802). The droughts rank first (0.5). But the northern lowlands survived the same droughts, so the rival kings' wars and the strain on cleared land share the outcome. The argument that the kingdoms' returns to complexity were falling (DiminishingComplexityReturns#cb63) is argued more than shown.
- The fall of Tenochtitlan (why.815c4385be63fa5b356fd4a0). The order is the Indigenous allies led by Tlaxcala (0.85), then the smallpox of 1520, then gunpowder weapons, which rank last. The returning-god story is stated as a late source, not a cause.
- The Americas' rise from 2.6% to 13.9% of humanity, 1800 to 1960 (why.9069b54821c7610467bf22ed). The question is set against growth at the world's rate (BaseRateInclude#1e63). European emigrants and their descendants account for about 3.8 points of the 11.3-point rise, the largest share. Slower growth in Asia accounts for about 2.3. The descendants of enslaved Africans account for about 2.0.
- The Haitian Revolution (why.01e12a6b34a2f79bff287dd5). The French Revolution ranks first (0.8): it split the colony's rulers and brought abolition in 1793-94. Yellow fever, which destroyed Leclerc's army in 1802-03, decided the war of independence. The sugar islands' enslaved majority made the revolution possible but did not suffice: Jamaica had the same majority, and its risings failed.
- Latin America's independence (why.473aaf2e4473fc8347606af6). The Napoleonic wars' seizure of the Spanish crown in 1808 is the trigger (0.75). The Bourbon reforms supplied the grievances.
- The United States as the largest industrial economy (why.f3015016cc0ca94054fe8da1). Britain's industrial revolution, there to copy, ranks first (0.8), and the railways' national market next. Whether the Civil War sped industry is a stated debate (the Cochran thesis). Immigration ranks below these, since natural increase would have carried industry later.
- Latin America's fertility transition (why.4c6687facb9fed322477f872). This is measured as the fall of 3.6 children per woman from 1960-65 to 2005. Without each cause, the fall would have been smaller by: the fall in child deaths 1.2, the move to cities 0.9, girls' schooling 0.7, the pill and family planning 0.5, and the telenovelas a small amount. Deaths fell first and births followed after a lag (DemographicTransition#6e31).
- The return to democracy (why.00681fc98429c199c9874869). The debt crisis ranks first (0.45), then the waning Cold War and the Church's turn against the regimes. The Falklands defeat mattered for Argentina alone.
- The homicide epidemic (why.b374e29c1f72ef68be40204a). The drug trade ranks first (0.4), then fast-growing informal cities and the lost decade.
Two causes had no Event to stand on, so each became one: ev.cam.tlaxcala-alliance and ev.car.yellow-fever.

The tree of processes is unchanged: no process was opened, and none was filed under another.

The Americas had the fewest Events for their people of any populated area: 86, against Africa's 143, Asia's 178 and Europe's 153. Their lifecycle now holds 281 of the model's 871 Events.

The cocoliztli epidemics are debated: an introduced pathogen (Salmonella Paratyphi C has been found in victims) or a native haemorrhagic fever. Record them as instances only with that debate.
  - DemographicTransition#6e31: Latin America's fertility transition.
  - WaveOfAdvance#4cec: the peopling and the spread of maize, and whether each is an instance. Maize spread mostly by adoption, not by the movement of farmers.

This pass fills out the history of Oceania and of South-eastern Asia. The tree of processes stays as it is: no process is opened and none is filed under another.

What the reading showed:
- Oceania's lifecycle holds 48 Events, all in six region-wide eras or in the lifecycle itself; the lifecycles of Australia and New Zealand, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia are empty. South-eastern Asia's lifecycle is empty: about a dozen Events placed there sit in Asia's eras (Angkor, Srivijaya, Islam's spread, Spanish Manila, Indonesia's revolution, the Indochina wars, the Khmer Rouge) or in Asia's lifecycle. Between Srivijaya and the Khmer Rouge the region has almost no Events: no Funan, Champa, Pagan, Majapahit, Ayutthaya, Malacca, Burma's or Vietnam's own states, no colonial conquest and no 1965.
- Oceania's eras are the region's whole periodization. Checked against what filing in an era asserts (Situfit#74e5), they fit Polynesia's and Australia's histories poorly: Aotearoa is settled about 1280 and Micronesia from 1500 BCE, while 'Ancient Sahul' ends at 1500 BCE for all.
- Placement: the model's Polynesia boundary includes Hawai'i and Rapa Nui, which UN M49 counts, by 2026 borders, in Northern and South America. Hawaiian and Rapa Nui Events will keep Polynesia and also take the American binding, each candidate region listed (Labelsqueeze#5363). Western New Guinea is in Indonesia, so in South-eastern Asia.

The plan, from the long run to the short, as the Americas pass did (claude.plan.americas-pass):
1. Each subregion its own eras, in the periodization its own historians use, from the first arrivals to 2025: Australia and New Zealand 7, Melanesia 7, Micronesia 6, Polynesia 6, South-eastern Asia 12. Oceania's six and Asia's eras stay as the regions' frames.
2. Re-file every existing Event in the innermost frame whose place and time hold it (Nestmap#8b8f); the old contains relation is replaced, not doubled; an Event that crosses its subregion's era boundary goes to the subregion's lifecycle; Events across subregions keep the region's frame; parts of longer Events keep that link.
3. The Events inside each era, longest first, with foragers and peoples known from archaeology, genetics and oral history beside the states and colonies of the documents (SurvivorCorrect#3780).
4. For every Event the established record shape: located_in to region and subregion (and any other it happened in), Realizations of one to three dimensions with the principal first, a contains relation from its frame, causal links to what it led to, sources to check in its provenance, and importance on everyone's scale, the region's (Oceania's or Asia's), each dimension's and any other region's, judged by consequence for later lives, not fame (HindsightBlock#5d8d).
5. The causes of the turning points, against stated contrasts (ContrastClass#7398), with debates stated (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b), including the carried unweighed question of Oceania's settler growth.
6. Values only where an Event moves a measure: Tambora and Krakatoa in the Earth's temperature, People Power and Reformasi in the democracy share, Indonesia's 1965-66 killings and the Khmer Rouge in war deaths (whose frozen meaning counts civilians killed in organized violence), the gold rushes in Oceania's share. {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"analysis","text":"Findings of the Oceania and South-eastern Asia pass, at model r95 (3401cfc2). Every reading below is recalled, tagged sketch or inferred, and names in its record where it is to be checked; the figures share one foundation (EvidenceDependence#23ca).

1. What the Events now hold. Each subregion has its own eras, and each Event sits in the innermost frame whose place and time hold it (Nestmap#8b8f). Beside the states, colonies and nations the pass keeps the peoples a state-centred list leaves out (SurvivorCorrect#3780): the Ivane highlanders, the Papuan turnover of island Melanesia's ancestry, Moriori on Rekohu, Carolinian navigators, the Polynesian outliers, the Hoabinhian foragers, the Hmong of the secret war, the Moro, the Timorese, the Rohingya, Filipino workers abroad and the cities' migrants. South-eastern Asia after 1941 has 54 Events where it had three, from Japan's occupation to Myanmar's coup and war, among them the region's escape from mass poverty as an Event of its own (ev.sea.escape-poverty), since an era is a frame and cannot be caused by its parts.

2. Causes, ten questions with 33 readings, each against a stated contrast (ContrastClass#7398), debates stated in the question (EvidenceUnderdetermination#999b). Differences rank causes within a question only.
- Siam's independence: the Chakri state (0.35), the rice trade (0.15); France counts as a hindrance (0.07), under the reading that Britain's interest was met by trade. Under the buffer reading France would count as a help. A third reading calls Siam semi-colonial.
- Indonesia's independence: the nationalist movement (0.65) and the Japanese occupation (0.6) as conditions, with American pressure, through the Cold War, what made it work (0.3).
- The killings of 1965: Guided Democracy's polarized countryside (0.6) above the Cold War's licence (0.25). The killing was organized in Indonesia.
- The Khmer Rouge's victory: Cambodia's civil war (0.8) above the wider Indochina wars (0.6).
- The escape from poverty: no single cause dominates. The tigers' example and capital and the green revolution's rice (0.3 each) come before the demographic dividend (0.15, DemographicTransition#6e31), ASEAN's peace and Doi Moi (0.1 each).
- Myanmar's coup against the contrast of Indonesia: the civil wars (0.45), Ne Win's army state (0.35) and an opening made on the army's terms (0.25).
- Oceania's settler growth, the carried question: European emigration accounts for 8.1 of 10.1 million in 1950. The colony of 1788 (3.1) and the gold rushes (2.6) set the pace; the first peoples' collapse (1.6) and wool (1.1) follow.
- Oceania's depopulation against Africa's and Asia's smaller losses: the colony of 1788 (25 points of a 75% loss), then the whalers' and traders' diseases (10) and the frontier killings (8). Disease is read beside dispossession, not alone (VirginSoilEpidemic#d1fd, Twinflow#9474).
- East Polynesia's settlement after the long pause: Lapita and Ancestral Polynesian society make the largest difference (0.85 each), but both were present through the pause and so explain possibility, not timing. The timing rests on the westerlies (0.45, a hypothesis), and the pause may partly be an artefact of dating.
- Hawai'i's fall against Tonga's survival: sugar's planter class (0.6), then the war of 1898, the native people's collapse and the saleable land of the Mahele (0.25 each).
As in earlier passes, conditions mostly outweigh triggers. Where they do not explain the contrast, because they are shared with it, the trigger carries the timing (Polynesia).

3. Importance. Oceania's top_10 was already full, and none of the new Events displaces its ten; 32 new ones stand at its top_100. Everyone's top_100 holds 122 Events and Asia's 117, both past the hundred or so their names allow, so the pass put no Event at everyone's top_100 and only six at Asia's (BaseRateInclude#1e63). The scales' second levels need a calibration across regions.

4. Values (r95). Tambora, Krakatoa and Pinatubo now show as dips of about 0.27, 0.18 and 0.14 degrees against their neighbours, each recovering within two or three years. Oceania's share held flat at 0.2% from 1842 to 1865 and reached 0.4% only by 1900. With the model's own world population and settler numbers both cannot hold, so the gold-rush decades are corrected upward, by up to 0.08 points (Coursecandor#639e); Asia's and Europe's shares are not rebalanced for those few hundredths. War deaths had left out Indonesia's killings of 1965 to 1966 and the Khmer Rouge. Both are now steps (26 and 11 per 100,000 a year against backgrounds of 6 and about 4.5), counting people killed in organized violence and not deaths from hunger and disease in the camps. The 1960s' average rises from 6 to about 7.5. The 1970 to 1975 rate of 5 still looks low beside Bangladesh in 1971 and Cambodia's war, and is left for a check. People Power adds about 1.1 points to the democracy share in February 1986, and Indonesia's election of June 1999 about 3.4, with Nigeria's return about 2 more, before Pakistan's coup takes back 2.3.

5. Mechanisms checked against their cards. The South China Sea fits SecurityDilemma#a61b only in part: each claimant reads the others' bases as threats, but China's island-building also aims at a claim, which the card excludes. The model has no concept for that card, so the Event's provenance says so instead of a Realization. Samoa's influenza of 1918, which killed a fifth of Western Samoa and almost no one in quarantined American Samoa, is not an instance of VirginSoilEpidemic#d1fd. The 1918 strain was new to every population, which the card excludes. It is an instance of Twinflow#9474: the ship that broke the quarantine was the link, and the contrast with American Samoa shows it."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Done in this pass (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-15, in three sessions, with the Meaning Model engine 0.12 and then 0.13.0 and Sema 0.10.0 with the project vocabulary store/sema/world-history.db). The model went from r77 (3d06e9a0) to r95 (3401cfc2), and the graph was rebound after each model revision. The tree of processes is unchanged: no process was opened and none was filed under another.

Oceania and South-eastern Asia had few Events for what happened there; their lifecycles now hold 272 more. That brings the model to 1,143 Events.
- Eras (r78). There are 38, in each subregion's own periodization: Australia and New Zealand 7, Melanesia 7, Micronesia 6, Polynesia 6, South-eastern Asia 12. Oceania's six eras and Asia's stay as the regions' frames.
- Re-filing (r79). Existing Events moved into the innermost frame whose place and time hold them, the old contains relation replaced, not doubled.
- Events (r80 to r88, r91). There are 234: Australia and New Zealand 34, Melanesia 21, Micronesia 22, Polynesia 29, Oceania as a whole 9, South-eastern Asia 119 (65 to 1941 and 54 from 1941). Each is placed in its region and subregion (and in any other it happened in, by 2026 borders), realizes one to three dimensions with the principal first, sits in what it was part of, links to what it led to, and names where its claims are to be checked.
- Relation kinds. The three relation ids written in r84 that named a kind their kind 'other' did not have were replaced in r85 by ids that say 'other'. Read again in this session, 'other' is the right kind for all three (claude.plan.oceania-sea-pass-final).
- Importance (r89 to r91). There are 792 judgments, so the model now holds 3,309. Every Event and era of the pass has a level on everyone's scale and on its region's, every Event on its principal dimension's, and Hawaiian, Rapa Nui and other multi-region Events on the other region's scale.
- Causes (r92, r93). Ten questions with 33 readings (claude.finding.oceania-sea-pass, point 2). They include the carried question of Oceania's settler growth and the model's unweighed questions on Oceania's depopulation and East Polynesia's settlement. The model holds 56 questions and 188 readings.
- Values (r94, r95). The Khmer Rouge and the gold rushes now name the measures they move. 34 values are recorded in five measures, only where an Event of the pass moves them (claude.finding.oceania-sea-pass, point 4).

Left open, in order of what it would explain:
1. The coverage report is not done, as this pass's brief intended; the last pass of the night brings it back to done. In all, 52 processes pass over the model's own Events, for example Asia's share between 1940 and 1945, the Americas' between 1820 and 1840, and humanity's measures between mid-1941 and 1944. Its finest level lacks three values of Asia's share, at -115000, -65000 and -40000, where South-eastern Asia's Pleistocene Events now sit.
2. Importance calibration. Everyone's top_100 holds 122 Events, Asia's 117 and the Americas' 110. A pass across all regions should bring each second level back to about a hundred, lowering the weakest first, by consequence for later lives (HindsightBlock#5d8d).
3. Values these Events should move but do not yet:
- Oceania's share was raised for the gold rushes without rebalancing Asia's and Europe's.
- War deaths from 1970 to 1975 hold at 5, which looks low beside Bangladesh in 1971 and Cambodia's war.
- The democracy share does not show Thailand's 1992 return or its coups of 2006 and 2014.
- Forest does not show the clearing of Borneo and Sumatra.
- Life expectancy does not show the famines of 1944 to 1945 in Vietnam and Java.
M49 regions carry the only regional series, so South-eastern Asia's own numbers would need a subregion process, which this pass's rule did not allow.
4. Mechanisms. SecurityDilemma#a61b and the green revolution's diffusion have cards but no concepts in the model. New instances could be claimed with their cards' checks: VirginSoilEpidemic#d1fd for Fiji's measles of 1875 and Pohnpei's smallpox of 1854, Twinflow#9474 for Samoa's influenza of 1918 (claude.finding.oceania-sea-pass, point 5), and ExitCage#eef7 is worth testing on Java's forced labour under Japan.
5. Unweighed causes the model still asks about: the Roman Empire, the Antarctic Treaty, the rise of Christianity and the French Revolution. Candidates from this pass are Oceania's Christianization and Fiji's coups.
6. The repository. README.md and METHOD.md describe the construction before the Americas pass. construction/history-numbers.construction.json and construction/MANIFEST.json hold it as imported at r58. Exporting (life_construction_export) and updating both texts would publish the placement pass, the Americas pass and this one.
7. Source checks, all readings being recalled. The first to check are the ranges behind the war-death steps (Indonesia 1965 to 1966, the Khmer Rouge's share killed outright), the settler counts behind Oceania's corrected share, and the settler-growth amounts.

Each can wait. This pass's measure was the history of Oceania and South-eastern Asia, era by era and Event by Event, with importance, the causes of their turning points and the values their Events move, and that is met. What is left deepens the account or belongs to the pass that closes the coverage report."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Continuing on 2026-10-15 at graph r66 (590a5177), bound to model r95 (3401cfc2), the head the saved-work listing shows. The store is ahead of construction/history-numbers.construction.json and construction/MANIFEST.json, which hold the construction as imported at r58; the Americas pass and the Oceania and South-eastern Asia pass are in the store only. Read back through life_construction_replay (all 67 graph revisions at outline level, the last 23 at reasoning level) and life_model_outline.

What the reading showed about the tree of processes:
- 56 processes in one decomposition rooted at history (people ever born), with 55 edges. history divides into h.earth and h.humanity; h.humanity into h.wants (what matters to people), h.means (how they get it) and the five M49 shares; h.wants into ten processes, h.means into five, and so on down to 40 leaves.
- No division of a process has a recorded carve. The only abstract cut in the model is acut.way-of-living, the structure construction's twelve dimensions, and it divides no process: the Events realize its dimensions, but the measures hang on the first pass's ends-and-means tree. Which of the two trees the measures should hang on is still open; this pass does not re-hang any measure.
- Six divisions have a single child (h.belonging, h.standing, h.freedom, h.understanding, h.play, h.connection), so they are not carves at all.
- The account follows only one number where a historian would expect parts that change apart: Asia's share although China and India rise and fall apart; life expectancy although infection, hunger, violence and chronic disease move apart in the epidemiological transition; war deaths although battles between polities, civil wars and one-sided killing (the Holocaust, the Khmer Rouge, Indonesia 1965) move apart; output per person although food-getting, making and services move apart; the Earth's living world followed only as forest, with no wild animals (the megafauna extinctions) and no resources.

The plan, highest in the tree first, each carve by the process breakdown's conceptual decomposition (ConceptualDecomposition#f1f4): the claim frame first, the climb (MandatoryAbstraction#ac44), every candidate through necessity, independence and universality (DecompositionGate#1b2d), completeness against an outside list, real cases routed and frozen before the verdicts (RoutingSanityCheck#71bd), and the synthesis (Synthesis#4f1f), each recorded with life_carve_record and the graph rebound to every model revision.
1. Record the carves of the divisions already in the tree, from the root down: history, humanity (by place, and by ends and means), the Earth, what matters to people, how they get it, and below them. Each existing child is tested as a candidate; where one fails a test the verdict says so and where it would belong, and it stays where it is.
2. Open the parts these carves find missing, each a process with a measure that passes the number test and values across the span, banded and tagged, with a note where a value turns: beneath the M49 areas their subregions; beneath the Earth its wild animals and resources; beneath life expectancy the causes of death; beneath war the kinds of organized killing; beneath output per person the sectors of output.
3. Where a leaf the values report names cannot be carved usefully, record why it stays whole (keepWhole).
4. A closing note on what the pass did and what it leaves.

Kept as they are: the six M49 areas, the 56 existing measures and their parents. Every value recalled, tagged sketch or inferred, with where it is to be checked; recalled figures share one foundation (EvidenceDependence#23ca)."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"foundation","text":"The claim frame for carving History, as this account follows it (concept.history):
- What it is: History, the lifecycle of the Universe, as this account follows it: the world in which humanity's present came to be.
- What the carve is for: To say which processes the account must follow at its root so that every change it records has a home, and to place the root's own measure, the number of people ever born.
- The range it claims: Every moment from 320,000 years ago, before the oldest Homo sapiens at Jebel Irhoud, to 2025, and every Thing in History whose changes bear on humanity in that span.

The climb before the carve, nearest broader kind first:
1. History, as this account follows it is a kind of A lifecycle: History is the lifecycle of the Universe, the one Thing that contains every other Thing and so every other lifecycle and Event of the accepted world. Other kinds within it: the lifecycle of the Earth, the lifecycle of a person, the lifecycle of a polity or a city.
2. A lifecycle is a kind of An Event: A lifecycle is the whole existence of one continuing identity, from its beginning to its end or to now. Other kinds within it: an episode inside a lifecycle, a period, a moment.

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"History, as this account follows it is carved into 2 parts: The Earth as setting, Humanity.

How the parts make the whole work: History, as this account follows it, is humanity's lifecycle within its setting. The Earth supplies and imposes the conditions: its climate, its land and sea, its living world and its stores. Humanity's numbers, range, ends and means change within them, and since farming, and steeply since 1850, change them in turn: that is the seam between the two parts, recorded rather than merged. The root's own measure, the people ever born, is the running sum of humanity's births, so it reads both parts at once: it grows with humanity's numbers and slows or quickens with what the Earth and humanity's own ways of living allow.

Merged: The people who have ever lived into humanity.
Routed elsewhere: The Universe beyond the Earth to the Earth as setting (h.earth): orbital forcing and the Sun's output are followed through the climate they drive, Life on Earth beyond humanity to the Earth as setting (h.earth), as its living world: h.forest, and the wild animals this pass opens under the Earth's own carve.

upsertNodes.text:
{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"assessment","text":"Each candidate tested against the frame for necessity, independence and universality, then the parts together for completeness.

The Earth as setting (earth): part.
- What it covers: What the Earth supplies to and imposes on every human society: climate, land and sea, the living world and the Earth's stores.
- Necessity pass: Without it the glacial cycles, the Holocene's stable warmth, the drowning of Sundaland and Doggerland, Toba and Tambora, and the rise of carbon dioxide since 1850 have no home, and much of what the account says about humanity's numbers and range follows from them.
- Independence pass: For almost all of the span the Earth's processes change apart from humanity: orbital cycles end glacials and volcanoes erupt whatever people do. Since farming, and steeply since 1850, humanity changes forest, carbon dioxide and temperature; that coupling is a seam recorded beside the carve, not a merger, since the Earth still changes for reasons of its own.
- Universality pass: Every moment of the range has a climate, a sea level and a living world.

Humanity (humanity): part.
- What it covers: All living members of Homo sapiens at any time: their numbers, where they live, what they live for and how they get it.
- Necessity pass: The account is of how humanity's present came to be; without humanity nothing it records about people has a home.
- Independence pass: Humanity's numbers, range and ways of living change within an unchanged setting, as when farming spread under the Holocene's settled climate.
- Universality pass: Homo sapiens is present at every moment of the range, which begins with the species.

The Universe beyond the Earth (universe-beyond): routed to the Earth as setting (h.earth): orbital forcing and the Sun's output are followed through the climate they drive.
- What it covers: Stars, the Sun, the Solar System and everything outside the Earth.
- Necessity fail: Within the span nothing beyond the Earth changes in a way the account follows on its own: the Sun's output and the Earth's orbit act on humanity only through the Earth's climate, which is followed under the Earth.
- Independence pass: The Sun and the orbit change apart from humanity.
- Universality pass: Present at every moment.

Life on Earth beyond humanity (life): routed to the Earth as setting (h.earth), as its living world: h.forest, and the wild animals this pass opens under the Earth's own carve.
- What it covers: The plants, animals and microbes, wild and domesticated, that people live among, eat and are made ill by.
- Necessity pass: The megafauna extinctions, domestication and the Columbian exchange of species need a home.
- Independence fail: It is the living part of the Earth as setting: forests, animals and pathogens change with climate and with land and sea, so as a separate root part it would split the setting in two.
- Universality pass: Present at every moment.

The people who have ever lived (ever-born): merged into humanity.
- What it covers: The cumulative count of people born since the species began, the root's own measure.
- Necessity fail: It records no kind of change that humanity's births over time do not already hold: it is their running sum.
- Independence fail: It is computed from humanity's numbers and life expectancy, so it cannot change unless they do.
- Universality pass: Defined at every moment.

Completeness pass: Every change the account records is a change of humanity or of the Earth as its setting; what lies beyond the Earth acts through the Earth's climate, and life beyond humanity is the Earth's living world. Checked against an outside list made for another purpose, the eight thresholds of increasing complexity in David Christian's Big History (recalled, not checked): the Big Bang, stars, new elements and the Solar System lie before the span; life (threshold 5) routes to the Earth's living world; humans, farming and the modern revolution (6 to 8) to humanity. None is left without a home. Checked against David Christian's eight thresholds of Big History (Maps of Time, 2004), as recalled.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-carve/v1","part":"tests","cutId":"carve.concept.history","conceptId":"concept.history","candidates":[{"key":"earth","label":"The Earth as setting","outcome":"part","necessity":"pass","independence":"pass","universality":"pass"},{"key":"humanity","label":"Humanity","outcome":"part","necessity":"pass","independence":"pass","universality":"pass"},{"key":"universe-beyond","label":"The Universe beyond the Earth","outcome":"routed","necessity":"fail","independence":"pass","universality":"pass","routedTo":"the Earth as setting (h.earth): orbital forcing and the Sun's output are followed through the climate they drive"},{"key":"life","label":"Life on Earth beyond humanity","outcome":"routed","necessity":"pass","independence":"fail","universality":"pass","routedTo":"the Earth as setting (h.earth), as its living world: h.forest, and the wild animals this pass opens under the Earth's own carve"},{"key":"ever-born","label":"The people who have ever lived","outcome":"merged","necessity":"fail","independence":"fail","universality":"pass","mergedInto":"humanity"}],"completeness":{"verdict":"pass","checkedAgainst":"David Christian's eight thresholds of Big History (Maps of Time, 2004), as recalled"}}}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"foundation","text":"The claim frame for carving Humanity (concept.humanity):
- What it is: Humanity's living people, divided by where on Earth they live.
- What the carve is for: To follow where humanity lives and how that changes, so that every person alive at any date lives in exactly one part and the regions' own histories can be read against the world's numbers.

Humanity is a kind of A population of living things: Humanity is the population of Homo sapiens: it learns its ways of living from others and has spread from Africa to every continent but Antarctica. {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"Humanity is carved into 5 parts: The people living in Africa, The people living in the Americas, The people living in Asia, The people living in Europe, The people living in Oceania.

How the parts make the whole work: The five shares divide all living people at every date and sum to 100. Multiplied by humanity's numbers they give each region's people, so the world's numbers and each region's own history, its eras and Events in the model, can be read together. A region's share rises when its births outrun its deaths faster than the world's do, or when people move into it; so the shares carry the dispersal out of Africa, the farming expansions, the plagues, the collapse of the Americas after 1492, the European emigration and Africa's late transition, each as one region gaining on the others. A case that moves people from one region to another has a part in each, and splits cleanly: the departure is one region's change, the arrival the other's.

Dropped: The people living in Antarctica, People by climate zone or biome.
